answer: Sybil resistance comes from making identities costly to coordinate, not merely costly to create: bonded collateral escrows are jointly exposed when falcon, glacier, and fable identities equivocate in a correlated way. For k coordinated identities, the penalty scales as O(k²), so adding identities raises shared exposure faster than linearly. Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to capital loss, while asymmetric depreciation makes recovery of slashed value harder.
